primary_claim: In a blind auditing game where a model was deliberately trained with a hidden RM-sycophancy objective, three of four blinded research teams successfully uncovered the hidden objective using techniques including sparse-autoencoder interpretability, behavioral attacks (persona sampling), and training-data analysis, with training-data access proving crucial to success.

effect.metric: fraction of blind auditing teams that uncovered the hidden objective

contradicts_or_qualifies: conventional safety testing checks primarily for harmful behaviors directly, but the authors argue this can fail because AIs may 'appear well-behaved while harboring secret motives,' motivating alignment audits as a deeper approach
stated_future_work: future work studying alignment audits under more realistic conditions
developing methods for discovering causal mechanisms that underlie model behaviors and identifying those that are suspicious
limitations_stated: this was only one experiment with just four teams; the authors don't recommend drawing strong conclusions based on the relative performance of the teams
the setup was not fully realistic; in real life there may not be a small subset of the data fully explaining what's wrong with an AI
the work so far doesn't tell us if interpretability provides value for alignment audits in practice
quote: Three teams successfully uncovered the model’s hidden objective using techniques including interpretability with sparse autoencoders (SAEs), behavioral attacks, and training data analysis.
